stem: The cartoonist’s main point is that

options.text: free labor had failed to improve the lives of Southern workers
options.misconception: The cartoon is pessimistic about free labor.

options.text: the Atlanta Exposition was a gathering for Confederate veterans only
options.misconception: Only Confederate veterans attend the fair.

options.text: emancipation had opened the way to a prosperous, industrial South
Northern investors had bought up all Southern land
options.misconception: The cartoon shows Northerners buying Southern land.

rationales.A: The mood is triumphant, not gloomy: “PROSPERITY” fills the sky.
rationales.B: The crowd mixes Black and white Southerners, veterans among them, heading to the fair.
rationales.C: The cartoon spells it out: a worker labeled “FREE LABOR” leads a crowd past Lincoln toward the exposition, under the word “PROSPERITY.” The artist links freedom to Southern progress.
rationales.D: No sale or investor appears; the image celebrates labor, not a buyout.
rationales.general:
1. Read the labels. “FREE LABOR” and “PROSPERITY” name the cartoon’s two ideas.
2. Follow the crowd. Black and white Southerners walk together past Lincoln toward the exposition.
3. Ask what connects them. Emancipation freed labor, and the cartoon says free labor builds prosperity.
4. Test the gloomy readings. Nothing in the image shows failure, a veterans-only meeting, or a land sale.
Remember: in a cartoon, the labels and the direction of the crowd carry the argument.

stimulus.source_note: Udo J. Keppler, “The New South — The Triumph of Free Labor,” Puck magazine, October 23, 1895. Public domain (Library of Congress).
stimulus.text: A large Black worker wearing a sash reading “FREE LABOR” stands with a hammer in one hand and a plow at his feet. Behind him, a crowd of Black and white Southerners, including Civil War veterans, walks past a statue of Abraham Lincoln toward a bright fairground. A flag reads “ATLANTA EXPOSITION,” and the word “PROSPERITY” shines in the sky above the fairground. The caption reads: “THE NEW SOUTH — THE TRIUMPH OF FREE LABOR.”
